    As above; host (the CPU constant, the host description and the parallel width, as the duel report prints them) is a paragraph of its own under the title, followed by the skipped-turns tally and, when the members' R records carried it, the duress tally (issue #102, BENCH-12).
    (package private) static String
    TeamReport.renderOpponent(Opponent o, String label, List<TeamReport.Battle> candidate, List<TeamReport.Battle> baseline, String robot, String baselineRobot, int rounds, int width, int height, String host)
    One opposing team's own report for the per-opponent bench strategy (issue #102): the seed-by-seed table (with the baseline's share and the paired difference when a baseline ran), then the members' team records (T) for the diagnostics: the engine's count of bullets that hit our own members, drives the teammate fence replaced, and each member's own counts.

    The paired A/B table, per opponent team (issue #102, BENCH-2's convention): the candidate's and the baseline's battle against the same team at the same seed, so noise common to both cancels.
